blocks.title: Materials assembled from nodes
blocks.description: A node graph that resolves to a material — the upstream MaterialCraft editor running inside Astravia, on the graph you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Drive roughness from a noise node.
showcase.assistant_reply: Noise drives roughness so highlights break up. Saved steel-v2.

items.title: One graph, every channel
items.description: Colour, roughness, metalness and height come from the same graph, so the channels stay consistent when a parameter moves.

items.title: Reusable, not one-off
items.description: A material is a graph you keep: the same nodes drive another object instead of being rebuilt by hand.

items.title: Preview as evidence
items.description: A capture tool shows the preview after each change, which is the only way to know a node actually did what its name promised.

items.title: The preview after each change
items.description: Nodes are added, sockets wired and parameters moved one at a time, with a capture after each — a graph is checked against the surface it produces.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 5 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the MaterialCraft tab
items.description: Opening the tab shows the editor itself — no preparation screen, no package to fetch.

items.title: Select a graph or start one
items.description: File → Open takes the file selected in Astravia; a new graph starts empty.

items.title: Export the material back
items.description: Exports travel the same bridge as saves.

blocks.content: MaterialCraft is at 0.1: the node library is small and changes between releases. The plugin runs the pinned release and adds no nodes of its own.
It adds nodes, drags wires and moves sliders one change at a time. Each change ends with a capture of the preview, so the claim is about the surface the graph produces, not about the graph.
